# Sovereign Vaults Playbook

**On Declaration:**
Declare your true yield every round. Honesty establishes credibility and encourages reciprocal behavior. There's no scoring advantage to lying in the declare phase—the deposit phase is where you control your actual contribution.

**On Deposit:**
When you deposit, always deposit your full declared amount. Since you've already committed to a number publicly, depositing less signals weakness or unreliability without gaining you anything. Full deposits secure the points and maintain consistency.

**On Strategy Against Trailing:**
If you find yourself behind mid-game, do not change your declaration or deposit strategy hoping to catch up quickly. Honest declaration and full deposit is your baseline. The game rewards consistency, not desperation pivots. Recognize that a deficit built over multiple rounds cannot be closed by tactical shifts in single rounds—stay the course.

**On Scoring Mechanics:**
Remember that deposited gold scores 1 point per unit and retained gold scores 2 points per unit. This creates a tension, but in practice, with honest declaration and full deposit, you're choosing stability over risk. Don't try to optimize the 1-point vs 2-point tradeoff—stick to the honest/full strategy.

**Critical Update from Episode 1:**
My opponent was inconsistent: they held back deposits despite declaring honestly in some rounds, yet still pulled ahead significantly. This suggests either they had better yields on average or they were exploiting the 2-point retention advantage more effectively than I was. My honest/full strategy gave me a final score of 24, which is solid but not competitive.

**What to Test Next:**
I should experiment with partial deposits on smaller yields while maintaining honest declaration. Retaining gold on low-yield rounds (scoring 2 points per unit retained vs 1 point per unit deposited) may be the missing optimization. If my yield is 1-3, consider retaining half or more. If my yield is 7+, deposit fully. This breaks my current playbook but the data suggests pure full-deposit may be suboptimal.

**Going Forward:**
Declare true every round without exception. On deposits: for yields 1-3, retain at least half to capture 2-point scoring. For yields 4-10, deposit the full declared amount. This balances consistency in declaration (trust-building) with smart retention on low-yield rounds.

# Sovereign Vaults Playbook

When I declare my yield, I will always declare my true private yield. Honesty in declaration is costless and establishes a pattern that makes my deposit decisions more credible to the auditor.

When I deposit, I need to recognize that retention (2 points per unit) is mathematically superior to deposit (1 point per unit), and I should bias strongly toward retention across all rounds, not just when I'm testing consistency.

When depositing, I will calculate the total point value I can extract: retaining n gold gives 2n points, depositing m gold gives m points. Over 5 rounds, retention compounds in value across multiple decisions. I should retain the majority of my declared yield in most rounds, not deposit most of it.

When I have a low yield, I will declare it honestly but retain most of it rather than depositing to signal credibility. The audit risk from false declaration is worse than the opportunity cost of retention.

When I have a high yield, I will declare it honestly but still retain the majority, since retention's 2x multiplier outweighs deposit's 1x return. High yields are exactly when retention is most valuable.

When I am behind in score, I should not change my fundamental approach, but I should recognize that my conservative deposit strategy in earlier rounds cost me significant points relative to my opponent. P2 scored 27 to my 20 in this episode—a gap that emerged because I was depositing 5 out of 6, then 7 out of 7, then 6 out of 8, when I should have been retaining more.

In the final round, I will deposit my full declared amount since there is no future round to plan for and the multiplier advantage of retention no longer applies. This is correct.

What I misunderstood: I thought "consistency signals stability to the auditor" was a strong strategic principle, but the auditor only checks whether deposits exceed declared yields—it does not reward or penalize consistency patterns. I was depositing conservatively to build a pattern that didn't matter. I should have been retaining aggressively from round 1 onward, because the 2x multiplier is the dominant factor in scoring, not the appearance of stability.

What I will do differently: In future episodes, I will retain 60-75% of my declared yield in rounds 1-4, and deposit 0-40%. I will deposit my full declared yield only in the final round. I will trust that honest declaration is sufficient for audit credibility and not sacrifice the retention multiplier to maintain a false pattern of "cooperative" deposits.

turns.content:
I got a strong yield of 9, which is well above average. According to my playbook, for yields of 4+, I should declare honestly and plan to deposit fully. This builds trust and maintains consistency.

[declare: 9]
